featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Golden Chimney offered a comfortable and enjoyable dining experience during our visit.

The ambience inside the restaurant was quite good, especially after entering from the outside summer heat into the air-conditioned seating area.

There happened to be an IPL match playing during the visit as well, which added a lively atmosphere without making the place feel too noisy or chaotic.

For drinks, I ordered a fresh lime water, which was refreshing and suited the weather well.

For starters, we ordered the Murgh Lasoni Tikka and Classic Chicken Chilly. Both dishes were enjoyable, though the Murgh Lasoni Tikka stood out more for its flavour and preparation.

For the mains, we had the Butter Chicken, which was well prepared and satisfying.

Service was good, seating was comfortable, and overall the restaurant provided a pleasant dine-in experience.

All in all, a good restaurant option in the Opera House / Lamington Road area for a relaxed lunch or dinner with decent food and ambience.

featured_reviews.name: Anmol Sanyasi
featured_reviews.review_text:
From the very first meal, Golden Chimney completely won us over. The food is absolutely delicious — every dish is rich in flavor, beautifully balanced, and full of authentic taste. You can truly taste Mumbai in the food — the spices, the freshness, and the variety all come together perfectly. Each bite felt thoughtfully prepared and full of character.
What made our experience even more special was the staff. They are incredibly gentle, kind, and genuinely thoughtful. The hospitality here stands out. They pay attention to every detail and make sure you feel comfortable and taken care of. Whether it was helping us choose dishes or checking in to make sure everything was perfect, their service was warm and sincere. We were visiting Mumbai from outside the city for just four days, and we ended up eating at Golden Chimney four out of five days — that says everything. When you find a place that combines amazing food with outstanding hospitality, you naturally want to return. Every time we came back, the quality was consistent and impressive.
The money we spent was absolutely worth it.
The portion sizes, the flavor, the cleanliness, and the service all reflect great value for the price.
It's rare to find a restaurant where both the food and the people leave such a lasting impression.
If you're in Mumbai and want authentic, flavorful food with heartfelt hospitality, Golden Chimney is a must-visit. We will definitely return the next time we are in the city.

featured_reviews.name: Anmol Sanyasi
featured_reviews.review_text:
We went to Flavors at Bay near Hotel Hira mainly because it was convenient for us. Unfortunately, the food was a big disappointment.

I understand that it’s a vegetarian restaurant and spices are an important part of Indian cooking, but spices should complement the meal — not completely overpower it. Everything we ordered tasted like it was just packed with masala and nothing else.

We ordered momos, and they were honestly the worst part of the meal. They didn’t taste like real momos at all. Instead of a proper filling, it felt like a dough ball stuffed with pure spices. The taste matched how it looked — just overwhelming masala with no balance. Coming from a Nepali background where we eat momos often, this was really disappointing.

The biryani was the same story. It was mostly spice with very little flavor or balance beyond that.

The service itself was good and the staff were polite. The location was convenient for us as well. However, the restaurant felt quite empty and overall the food experience was not good. Unfortunately, the heavy spices even gave us heartburn afterwards.

We really wanted to enjoy the meal, but it ended up being a very disappointing experience.

On reminding the new staff (as old staff had vanished), they punched in repeat item in our bill, even though delivery happened only once! Due to their poor service I had to pay for an extra Juice! Not a nice experience.
When we are big group, and several guests have multiple choice of food, it is difficult for us to track but I would expect the restaurant staff to be able to handle accurate billing for large group of guests.

On discussing the same with owner (Rahul Jain), he said he will look in the CCTV footage and refund my amount via UPI. On following up, he said he did not get time but will refund the amount. I shared him 2 different UPI however both time he said incorrect UPI.
Later he changes his statement that no extra payment was charged! And then again he says that visit our restaurant where he can pay me in cash.
Looking at this behaviour, i will not like to even like to recommend this place to anyone.

Service - 3.5/5
Price - ₹400 for 2 people

The most critical failure of the visit was the Misal Pav.
• Misal Pav: 1/10
This was, quite frankly, one of the worst Misal Pavs I have ever encountered. It lacked the characteristic spice, texture, and authentic flavor profile that defines this Maharashtrian staple. It was sweet 😂. If Misal is your purpose for visiting, please look elsewhere.
• Other Dishes: 3/10 (Okish)
We also sampled the Sabudana Wada, Vatana Pattice, and Veg Biryani. While these items were merely "okish," they still scored a very low 3 out of 10. They lacked freshness, or any distinguishing quality to warrant a recommendation or even a second thought.
Ambiance and Facilities
On a positive note, the restaurant offers good sitting options, including both AC and Non-AC sections, which is a rare plus point in this category.
However, the facility challenges are severe:
• Parking: There is no dedicated parking available, which can be a significant hassle in the congested Girgaon area.
• Toilets: The washroom facilities were, without exaggeration, the worst. This is a major area needing immediate attention and upkeep.
Final Recommendation
If your goal is to experience good, authentic, and delicious Maharashtrian cuisine, do not visit Vinay. You will be better served by traveling a little further to established names.
Alternative Recommendations for Authentic Maharashtrian Food:
• Misal Pav: For a truly great Misal, visit Mamledar Misal (Thane).
• General Maharashtrian Cuisine: For excellent, reliable snacks and meals, Prakash Shuddh Upahar Kendra (Dadar) remains a gold standard.

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Golden Star is one of those rare Mumbai institutions that reminds you why some restaurants endure for generations. Nestled in the heart of Charni Road, this iconic establishment has built a legacy not through trends or reinventions, but through consistency, hospitality, and food that continues to comfort and delight.
The experience begins the moment the thali arrives at your table … a vibrant spread that celebrates the richness and diversity of Gujarati and Rajasthani cuisine. Every bowl, every accompaniment, and every freshly prepared item feels thoughtfully crafted. From the subtly sweet dals and perfectly balanced vegetables to the soft rotis, fluffy farsan, and indulgent desserts, each element contributes to a meal that is both wholesome and deeply satisfying.
What stands out most is the attention to detail. The flavours are authentic without being overwhelming, allowing the quality of the ingredients and traditional recipes to shine. The unlimited servings embody the warmth and generosity that are at the heart of Indian hospitality, encouraging diners to savour the meal at their own pace.
Equally commendable is the service. The staff are attentive, courteous, and remarkably efficient. Despite the restaurant’s popularity and steady flow of guests, the team maintains a personal touch, ensuring that every diner feels welcomed and well looked after. Plates are replenished promptly, requests are handled with a smile, and the overall experience feels genuinely hospitable rather than transactional.
Beyond the food, Golden Star carries with it a sense of history and nostalgia. It is more than just a restaurant … it is a cherished part of Mumbai’s culinary heritage. Generations of families have dined here, creating memories around the same tables and returning for the same familiar flavours year after year. That enduring legacy is felt in every aspect of the dining experience.
In a city constantly chasing the next big thing, Golden Star remains a shining example of how timeless food, impeccable service, and unwavering commitment to quality can create something truly special. A meal here is not merely lunch or dinner it is a celebration of tradition, hospitality, and the enduring spirit of Mumbai’s dining culture.
Highly recommended for anyone looking to experience one of the city’s most beloved and enduring culinary landmarks.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Golden Star Thali is a must-visit destination for all vegetarian thali enthusiasts, conveniently located right opposite Charni Road Station in Mumbai. This gem offers an authentic dining experience with its Marwadi and Gujarati cuisine that will leave your taste buds delighted.

From the moment you step in, the warm and welcoming ambiance sets the tone for a delightful meal. The staff at Golden Star Thali are not only attentive but also very cooperative, ensuring that every dish is served fresh and hot, just the way it should be.

The thali here is a true feast for the senses, offering a wide variety of flavors and textures. It includes an assortment of chutneys and pickles, along with a refreshing salad to start with. You are then treated to two delicious farsans – the soft and spongy khaman dhokla and the seasonal special batana ghughra, both prepared to perfection.

The sweet section of the thali is equally impressive, featuring a delightful fruit salad and the indulgent malpua. When it comes to the main course, you’re in for a treat with four different sabzis – the seasonal favorite surti undhiyu, the tangy sev tomato, the rich and creamy paneer capsicum, and the hearty choli (black-eyed beans).

Complementing these are the khati meethi dal, the comforting kadhi, and a choice of rice or khichdi. The variety of breads served, including fulka, puri, bhakri, and bajri rotla, ensures that you can savor each dish in its traditional accompaniment. And if that wasn’t enough, the dal baati churma and dal pakwan add an extra layer of authenticity and indulgence to the meal.

Priced between Rs. 590 and Rs. 650, the thali offers excellent value for money, considering the variety and quality of dishes served. Golden Star Thali is truly a perfect place for a family outing, where you can enjoy a sumptuous meal in a comfortable setting. Whether you're a fan of traditional flavors or just looking to explore the richness of Gujarati and Marwadi cuisine, this restaurant is a fantastic choice for a fulfilling dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Jatin Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Iconic restaurant located at Charni Road, perhaps needs no introduction, was in the vicinity and was craving for some yummy Chaat and fast food! Shiv Krishna was our stop for that night. Named after two deities, one can expect it to be an all veg restaurant. The moment you enter the restaurant you can see beautiful paintings of Lord Krishna in various a avatars all over. Restaurant has two levels, upper deck has AC.

Talking about what all we had at Shiv Krishna -

As mentioned earlier was craving for some Chaat so we started with Sev Puri. Neatly presented to us. Sev Puri is usually famous of all street vendors and hawkers in Mumbai but you get a similar taste of it sitting in the comforts of this place. We followed it up with Veg Pizza. I would personally say it's made in the Indian way and I have no qualms in saying that I love the pizza made in this style. Very homely style and I enjoyed it.

Along with food, we ordered for couple of drinks - Paan Mojito and Kit Kat Shake. Mojito was refreshing with fresh Paan flavor. Good part is no essence. Kit Kat Shake was decent. Moving on, we next tried the famous Pav Bhaji of Shiv Sagar. It definitely features amongst the top selling list and most popular dish. Again presented in a very neat way. Was pretty stuffed by now, but the manager suggested us to also try the Tandoori Cheese Kulcha which is a relatively new dish introduced by the restaurant. Served in a starter format, so quite unique in its way. Stuffing is a mix of paneer and cheese mashed well and grilled well. Stuffed in Kulcha covering and kept in tandoor. Would recommend people to try this dish in case they haven't tried it elsewhere.

Last but not the least, was really excited to have the Cassatta ice-cream. Have had it really long back and was excited to see it as a part of the menu here. A combo of chocolate, tutti fruti, butter scotch ice-cream with nuts used for garnishing. Just loved the ice-cream and would love to revisit the place just for this again.

featured_reviews.name: Monica
featured_reviews.review_text:
Revival is one of those places that quietly delivers on everything you expect from a comforting dining experience. With its sea facing setting and focus on Pure Veg and Jain food, it is a spot that naturally lends itself to relaxed family outings.

A recent visit was centred around their Summer Special Mango Menu, which brings in a refreshing seasonal touch. The Kairi Kanda Roomali and Pakoda made for a great start and disappeared almost instantly. The Paneer Kairi Tikka stood out with its soft texture and well balanced flavours, easily one of the highlights from the menu.

The beverage selection complements the theme well. Options like the Mango Frozen Margarita and Mango Passion Fruit Mojito are refreshing, while the Mango Lassi is a great pick if you are in the mood for something richer and more filling.

Moving to the mains, the Paneer Khada Masala with Garlic leaves a strong impression and ranks among the better versions you will come across. It fits perfectly into the kind of comforting, flavourful food this place is known for.

Desserts keep things traditional and satisfying. The Gulab Jamun paired with Lacchedar Rabdi works beautifully, while the Aamras Puri is an easy choice, especially during the season.

What makes Revival stand out is how easy it is to return to. It is the kind of place that works just as well for a casual meal as it does for a family outing, and even welcomes your furry companions.

Conveniently located a short walk from Charni Road station, and set within a heritage building just off the Chowpatty seaface, it is a spot that is both accessible and consistently dependable when you are in the mood for good, comforting food.

We explored a variety of cuisines with mixed results:

Mains & Breads: The Cheese Garlic Naan (5/5) was a highlight, and the Barabanki Kofta (4/5) offered great flavor. A special mention to the Butter Rumali Roti (5/5), which comes in a very generous portion.ra

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Nayan Bheda
featured_reviews.review_text:
Disappointing Experience on Diwali
We were a group of 5 who had booked a table a day in advance through Google for 20th Oct, 9pm. On calling the restaurant in the afternoon about parking, the manager suddenly claimed they have “stopped online reservations” — even though the slot was available and confirmed on Google. When I asked his name (atleast thriceA) he disconnected the call without telling.
Not taking a chance, we reached at 7:30pm. The restaurant was barely 40% occupied. Our waiter Kabir was polite and helpful — full marks to him for service.
The major issue happened at billing — they flatly refused to accept Zomato payment despite Zomato showing a good discount option. There was no notice displayed, and we were not told at entry or while ordering. The manager “Shrikant Pedhnekar” was unapologetic and defensive instead of clarifying or expressing regret. While we were leaving, another manager (name unknown) also argued with us. In this era of 'Customer First', not once these managers showed any signs of being apologetic nor regret. The high-handed attitude spoiled our mood. Especially when the prices are comparable with premium restaurants. While prices match that of premium restaurant, the customer-centric attitude does not.

Other aspects:
• Ambience feels dated — furniture and décor easily 15–20 years old
• Prices are comparable to premium restaurants but food is only average in taste and portion
• We ordered for two cocktails but they were not well made.
• Service charge of 10% was added automatically while most restaurants of this level charge 5% (we got it removed)
• Restaurant is on 1st floor - No lift so elderlies and people with mobility issues will find it difficult to reach the restaurant

Overall, good food and smiling service of Kabir the waiter saved complete disaster. One star is for him. 4 stars goes out for an unprofessional and disappointing handling of guests. Would not recommend until management fixes confirmed reservations, billing transparency and how they treat their customers.

The restaurant is well-suited for families, couples, and even pet owners, which adds a unique and welcoming touch.

The pure vegetarian and Jain food options are thoughtfully prepared, fresh, and full of flavor. Every dish feels hygienic and light, yet satisfying. The staff is polite, attentive, and ensures a smooth dining experience from start to finish.

Overall, it’s a perfect place to enjoy peaceful meals with great views, good service, and a warm atmosphere. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a clean, serene, and enjoyable vegetarian dining spot.

featured_reviews.name: Prachiraj Shrivastava
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mumbai Bites in Girgaon is a great spot if you love tasty street-style food with a clean and comfortable vibe. The menu has a lot of options—from classic chaats and sandwiches to Indo-Chinese and quick snacks—so it’s perfect whether you want a light bite or a full meal.

The food is flavourful, especially their pav dishes, fries, and shakes. Portion sizes are good for the price, and the presentation feels fresh. The staff is friendly and the service is fairly quick, even during busy hours. The place is small but nicely maintained, making it a good hangout spot with friends.

Overall, Mumbai Bites Girgaon gives a fun and satisfying café experience at reasonable rates.

featured_reviews.review_text: No seating option available. Only plastic tables to seat on the footpath. Cheese chilli toast was just bland to taste & average experience. The melting cheese sandwich was something worth trying. The blossom shakes here are value for money.

featured_reviews.name: About every Damnthing
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visit this once and you will make this place as your adda thats for sure!
.

1) Pahadi grill cheese sandwich - Very huge grill cheese sandwich with two chutneys and very tasty sandwich. Beautifully presented and was very tasty plus not too costly as well! Considering girgaon and sobo its way too affordable as well!
.
2) freyo tower - Their freyo tower starts from ₹150/- can you just believe that. Plus on top you get 3 options cheese corn balls, fries and nachos and in drinks you can choose mocktails, shakes or juices! I will recommend you to try this out for sure!
.
3) Gravy Khichiya - The best khichiya because not the ones u get from stalls or streets but the gravy can make u full easily and very tasty as well, very unique and highly recommended.
.
4) Aloo chilly - Paneer chilly sab jagah milta he try their aloo chillly omg its cery tasty and you will definitely love this as much as u love paneer chilly . A better alternative to those who are vegan.
.
Must visit this place, rates are affordable taste is amazing and hygiene is maintained.

.
.

.
